newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller says early polls on the agenda.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller says early polls on the agenda.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said on Wednesday early polls were on top of Turkey's agenda amid a rift in the ruling coalition over Islamist activism.
"An agenda with elections at the top of it has emerged. The solution is with the people," she told a meeting of her True Path Party MPs.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's government has slowly been crumbling since the army began pushing it to crack down on Islamist activism in February.

The conservative coalition partner True Path is to debate pulling out of the coalition with Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, at a series of meetings in the coming days, party officials said earlier.
Turkish press reports said Ciller would ask the party for the authority to demand that Erbakan hand over power to her soon to take the country to early elections. Polls are due by the year 2000.
Erbakan and Ciller, also the foreign minister, are due to swap jobs next year under a power-sharing deal.
